groups.name: Meta
groups.description: Names shown in the game's car list. The name suffix tells your tuned car apart from the stock car.

groups.name: Display
groups.description: Numbers shown on the car's spec sheet in the menus. They are text only and do not change how the car drives.

groups.name: Engine
groups.description: Power, rev limit and throttle behaviour of the engine. The power scale multiplies the whole torque curve.

groups.name: Turbo
groups.description: Boost pressure of the turbos. Only cars whose engine has a turbo show these. The boost of each turbo is the real cap; the engine-level maximum is only a reference.

groups.name: Gearbox & clutch
groups.description: Gear ratios, shift times and the automatic shifter, plus the clutch torque. A higher ratio number is a shorter gear.

groups.name: Differential
groups.description: Setup defaults of the differential as offered in the in-game setup (power, coast, preload). In the game the setup values count, they override the hardware values of the car files.

groups.name: Differential (hardware)
groups.description: The differential model in the car's drivetrain file: type and lock factors. A lock factor is a multiplier of the input torque (1.0 is 100%), preload is in Nm. The setup values override these.

groups.name: Steering
groups.description: Steering ratio and steering lock. The lock is measured from the centre to full lock, so the full range is twice the value. A negative ratio is needed when the steering arm sits behind the wheel centre.

groups.name: Brakes
groups.description: Total brake torque and the front/rear bias. The total torque is split by the current bias; the bias of the setup overrides the car file.

groups.name: Vehicle (hardware)
groups.description: Mass of the car as the physics uses it. A different mass shifts the weight balance and ride height; the stored spring collar positions are not recomputed by this tuner.

groups.name: Springs & anti-roll
groups.description: Spring rates and anti-roll bar stiffness of the setup, with the limits of the in-game setup screen. The setup values override the coilover values of the car files.

groups.name: Ride height & bump stops
groups.description: Target ride height, spring collar positions and bump stops of the setup. Kunos: the editor's Auto Setup computes the collar positions from the ride height, so change them by hand only together and test the result.

groups.name: Dampers
groups.description: Slow and fast damper rates of the setup. Cars with active dampers ignore these values, and cars with racing damper tables may use click numbers instead of force values: check this on the car.

groups.name: Suspension (physical)
groups.description: Spring, damper and anti-roll values stored in the car files themselves (coilover files). The setup values override most of them; they still matter inside the simulation of that file.

groups.name: Alignment & tyres
groups.description: Camber, toe, caster and tyre pressure of the setup, with their limits. A setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit by the game, which can make the car behave wrongly: keep value and limits consistent.

groups.name: Tyres
groups.description: Tyre model values of the car's own tyre files. Kunos advises against editing them: the code connecting them is not user-controlled and a changed calibration can make a tyre behave unpredictably. Change little and test.

groups.name: Fuel
groups.description: Fuel at the start of a session. Fuel weight changes the balance of the car.

groups.name: Electronics
groups.description: Traction control and ABS levels. Levels are counted from 0 (the first level); the car must define the first level as no intervention for the aid to be switchable off.

settings.label: Variant name
settings.description: Name of the car's preset/variant (value of the line whose key ends with _preset_base in en.cars.loc written by the build). The default is the stock car's own text for that line, you can change it. Shown only for cars whose stock text has such a line (cars without one get no variant line). Where exactly the game shows it is not confirmed.

settings.label: Name suffix
settings.description: Text appended to the stock car's name to form the name of the tuned car in the game's car list. The default _MY sorts the tuned car next to the stock car. 1 to 30 characters.

settings.label: Displayed power
settings.description: Power value on the car's spec sheet (car_specs POWER of the mechanical preset). Display text only, it does not change the engine: use power_scale for that. Kunos documentation: numeric specs appear in the main menu car selection and in the technical specs at the bottom of the mechanical presets, and are display values. The file stores the unit as HORSEPOWER_US.

settings.label: Displayed torque
settings.description: Torque value on the car's spec sheet (car_specs TORQUE of the mechanical preset). Display text only, it does not change the engine. Kunos documentation: numeric specs appear in the main menu car selection and in the technical specs at the bottom of the mechanical presets, and are display values.

settings.label: Rev limiter
settings.description: Engine rev limiter (EngineData.limiter). The engine cuts power when it reaches this speed. Kunos documentation: Limiter is the maximum rpm of the engine. nominal_rpm and engine_damage_rpm are separate settings and should normally be raised together with the limiter.

settings.label: Idle rpm
settings.description: Lowest engine speed (EngineData.minimum). Kunos documentation: Minimum is the stall rpm of the engine. Whether it also sets the idle speed is not confirmed in the game.

settings.label: Power scale
settings.description: Multiplies the torque value of every point of the engine power curve. 1.0 is stock, 1.056 is about +20 hp. Kunos documentation: power and torque values in the engine file are values at the wheel; the power curve is torque in Nm over rpm, and turbos multiply on top.

settings.label: Nominal rpm
settings.description: Nominal (peak) engine speed reference of the engine (EngineData.nominal_rpm). The stock value equals the rev limiter. What the game uses it for is not confirmed.

settings.label: Engine damage rpm
settings.description: Engine speed above which the engine takes damage (EngineData.damage.rpmDamageThreshold). Raise it together with the rev limiter, otherwise running at the new limiter damages the engine.

settings.label: Limiter cut frequency
settings.description: Frequency of the rev limiter cut (EngineData.limiterCycles). Kunos documentation: Limiter Cycles is the limiter frequency and works together with the engine inertia, the coast torque and the power torque. The effect in the game is not confirmed.

settings.label: Engine inertia
settings.description: Rotational inertia of the engine (EngineData.inertia). Assumed: a higher value makes the engine speed rise and fall more slowly, not confirmed.

settings.label: Throttle lag up
settings.description: Throttle response lag when the throttle is opened (EngineData.throttle_lag_up). Kunos documentation: the throttle lag delays the effect of the pedal input. The scale is not confirmed. The engine map also stores its own value, which this setting does not change.

settings.label: Throttle lag down
settings.description: Throttle response lag when the throttle is closed (EngineData.throttle_lag_dn). Kunos documentation: the throttle lag delays the effect of the pedal input. The scale is not confirmed. The engine map also stores its own value, which this setting does not change.

settings.label: Coast scale
settings.description: Multiplies the value of every point of the engine coast (off-throttle) curve. From about 1000 rpm upwards the stock points are negative, so a higher factor means stronger engine braking there; the positive points at low rpm are scaled too. 1.0 is stock. Kunos documentation: the coast curve has the same axes as the power curve (torque in Nm over rpm) but negative torque; it is 0 at idle rpm, and about 20 is the starter torque and the engine stall resistance. The effect of the factor in the game is not confirmed.

settings.label: Turbo 1 max boost
settings.description: Maximum boost pressure of the first turbo (TurboData.max_boost, in bar), written to the engine file, the turbo's own file and the car's inline copy. Kunos documentation: Max boost is the peak boost of a turbo; with two turbos each needs its own controller, or one runs unregulated at full boost. Not confirmed in the game. Shown only when the stock data has this field. Only shown for cars with a turbo.

settings.label: Turbo 2 max boost
settings.description: Maximum boost pressure of the second turbo (TurboData.max_boost, in bar), written to the engine file, the turbo's own file and the car's inline copy. Kunos documentation: Max boost is the peak boost of a turbo; with two turbos each needs its own controller, or one runs unregulated at full boost. Not confirmed in the game. Shown only when the stock data has this field. Only shown for cars with two turbos.

settings.label: Engine max boost
settings.description: Engine-level reference value of the turbo boost pressure in bar (EngineData.max_turbo_boost), written to the engine file and the car's inline copy. Kunos documentation: Max Turbo Boost has no physical effect, it is only a reference for gameplay and audio; the boost of each turbo (turbo_boost_1, turbo_boost_2) is the real cap. Only shown for cars whose engine lists a turbo file.

settings.label: Final drive ratio
settings.description: Final drive ratio. A higher number shortens every gear: stronger acceleration, lower top speed.

settings.label: Gear 1 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 1st gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing.

settings.label: Gear 2 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 2nd gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing.

settings.label: Gear 3 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 3rd gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing.

settings.label: Gear 4 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 4th gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing.

settings.label: Gear 5 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 5th gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing.

settings.label: Gear 6 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 6th gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing. Only shown for cars with at least 6 gears.

settings.label: Gear 7 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 7th gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing. Only shown for cars with at least 7 gears.

settings.label: Gear 8 ratio
settings.description: Gear ratio of 8th gear. A higher number gives shorter gearing. Only shown for cars with 8 gears.

settings.label: Auto-shift up rpm
settings.description: Engine speed at which the automatic gearbox shifts up (GearBoxData.autoshifter.up). Kunos documentation: Auto Shifter Up is the target rpm for the upshift. Raising it makes the automatic hold each gear longer; keep it below the rev limiter.

settings.label: Upshift time
settings.description: Duration of an upshift (GearBoxData.gear_up_time). Kunos documentation: Gear Up Time is the shift duration in ms. A lower value gives faster shifts.

settings.label: Downshift time
settings.description: Duration of a downshift (GearBoxData.gear_dn_time). Kunos documentation: Gear Dn Time is the shift duration in ms. A lower value gives faster shifts.

settings.label: Auto cut-off time
settings.description: Time the engine power is cut during an automatic shift (GearBoxData.auto_cut_off_time). Kunos documentation: Auto Cut Off Time is the length of the throttle cut. The unit (assumed milliseconds) is not confirmed. A lower value shortens the power cut.

settings.label: Diff power lock
settings.description: Default setup: how strongly the rear differential locks the rear wheels under throttle (0 = open, 1 = fully locked). Raising it makes both rear wheels turn together more, which helps keep the rear sliding on power.

settings.label: Diff coast lock
settings.description: Default setup: how strongly the rear differential locks the rear wheels when off throttle (0 = open, 1 = fully locked). Raising it keeps the rear locked together when you lift off the throttle.

settings.label: Diff preload
settings.description: Default setup: torque that always holds the differential locked, independent of throttle. Raising it locks the rear wheels together more even at low load.

settings.label: Diff power max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest value allowed for the differential power lock. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Diff coast max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest value allowed for the differential coast lock. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Diff preload max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest value allowed for the differential preload. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Differential type
settings.description: Differential hardware model (DifferentialData.type). Spool is a fully locked rear axle, the drift classic. The stock file does not store this field, so it reads as the first choice, LSD. Kunos documentation: the differential type can be changed on the fly (for example from LSD to Torsen) to get the desired effect; wear and temperature of the differential are ignored (not active). Not confirmed that the game applies it for this car.

settings.label: Diff preload (hardware)
settings.description: Preload torque of the differential model (DifferentialData.preload), written to the drivetrain file and the car's inline copy. These are the physical differential model parameters of the drivetrain file; the setup values diff_power_default, diff_coast_default and diff_preload_default are the in-game setup defaults. Kunos documentation: the preload is in Nm. Which layer the game uses is not confirmed.

settings.label: Diff torque bias power
settings.description: Torque bias ratio under power of the differential model (DifferentialData.torque_bias_ratio_power). Kunos documentation: Torsen differentials use the TBR (torque bias ratio), where 5.0 means 5:1. Assumed: a higher ratio locks the axle harder under power. Stock values differ per car; a car that does not store the field shows it as absent. These are the physical differential model parameters of the drivetrain file; the setup values diff_power_default, diff_coast_default and diff_preload_default are the in-game setup defaults. Which layer the game uses is not confirmed.

settings.label: Diff torque bias coast
settings.description: Torque bias ratio on coast of the differential model (DifferentialData.torque_bias_ratio_coast). Kunos documentation: Torsen differentials use the TBR (torque bias ratio), where 5.0 means 5:1. Assumed: a higher ratio locks the axle harder off throttle. Stock values differ per car; a car that does not store the field shows it as absent. These are the physical differential model parameters of the drivetrain file; the setup values diff_power_default, diff_coast_default and diff_preload_default are the in-game setup defaults. Which layer the game uses is not confirmed.

settings.label: Diff lock power (hardware)
settings.description: Lock factor under power of the differential model (DifferentialData.power). Kunos documentation: the power and coast locking is a decimal multiplier of the input torque (1.0 = 100%); the range 0 (open) to 1 (locked) is assumed. Stock values differ per car; a car that does not store the field shows it as absent (created when you set it). These are the physical differential model parameters of the drivetrain file; the setup values diff_power_default, diff_coast_default and diff_preload_default are the in-game setup defaults. Which layer the game uses is not confirmed.

settings.label: Diff lock coast (hardware)
settings.description: Lock factor on coast of the differential model (DifferentialData.coast). Kunos documentation: the power and coast locking is a decimal multiplier of the input torque (1.0 = 100%); the range 0 (open) to 1 (locked) is assumed. Stock values differ per car; a car that does not store the field shows it as absent (created when you set it). These are the physical differential model parameters of the drivetrain file; the setup values diff_power_default, diff_coast_default and diff_preload_default are the in-game setup defaults. Which layer the game uses is not confirmed.

settings.label: Steering ratio
settings.description: Default setup: steering wheel angle divided by front wheel angle. A lower number means quicker steering and less wheel turning for the same front wheel angle. Kunos documentation: the steer ratio should match the real car, and must be negative if the steering arm is behind the wheel centre.

settings.label: Steering ratio min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest steering ratio allowed (quickest steering). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Steering ratio max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest steering ratio allowed (slowest steering). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Steering rod ratio
settings.description: Steering rod ratio of the car (SteerControlsData.linearSteerRodRatio, stored in the .car only): front wheel angle per steering movement. Raising it gives more front wheel angle for the same hand movement (BMW stock 0.0017, the other tested cars 0.001975 to 0.0022). Kunos documentation: the linear steer rod ratio matches the steering wheel lock to the tyre lock. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Front caster
settings.description: Default setup: caster angle of the front wheels (both wheels). The stock values are small negative numbers and the unit is assumed to be degrees, not confirmed; the effect on the steering in the game is not confirmed.

settings.label: Brake bias front
settings.description: Default setup: share of the braking force sent to the front axle. Lowering it moves braking to the rear, which makes the rear lock up and rotate sooner. Kunos documentation: the Front Bias of the brake file is overwritten by the setup (and by the cockpit adjustment when the car has one).

settings.label: Brake bias min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest front brake bias allowed. The stock file does not store this field, so it reads as 0. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Brake bias max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest front brake bias allowed. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Brake bias front (brake file)
settings.description: Front brake bias stored in the brake file (BrakesData.frontBias), written to the brake file and the car's inline copy; the setup default brake_bias is separate. Kunos documentation: this Front Bias is overwritten by the setup (and by the cockpit adjustment when the car has one). Most cars store a percentage (for example 68), some store a fraction (for example 0.75); which of the two the game reads is not confirmed.

settings.label: Clutch max torque
settings.description: Maximum torque the clutch transmits before it slips (ClutchData.clutch_max_torque), written to the clutch file and the car's inline copy. A lower value should let the clutch slip earlier, a higher one hold more torque; effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Handbrake torque
settings.description: Braking torque of the handbrake (BrakesData.handBrakeTorque). Raising it locks the rear wheels harder when the handbrake is pulled, which helps start a slide.

settings.label: Total brake torque
settings.description: Total braking torque of the brake system (BrakesData.totalTorque). Raising it makes the brakes stronger. Kunos documentation: Total Torque is the total brake capacity, split front and rear by the current bias.

settings.label: Steering lock
settings.description: Steering lock of the car (SteerControlsData.steer_lock, stored in the .car only). Assumed to be degrees of steering wheel rotation, not confirmed. Kunos documentation: Steer lock is the angle from the centre to the maximum lock, so the total range is twice this value. Raising it allows more wheel rotation, and with it more front wheel angle.

settings.label: Car mass
settings.description: Physics mass of the car (GeneralCarData.totalMass, stored in the .car only). The displayed weight on the spec sheet is separate text. Raising it makes the car heavier to accelerate, brake and turn.

settings.label: Front anti-roll bar
settings.description: Default setup: stiffness of the front anti-roll bar. Stiffer means less body roll at the front and more understeer. Kunos documentation: the setup overwrites the anti-roll bars of the car file, unless ARB controllers are defined.

settings.label: Rear anti-roll bar
settings.description: Default setup: stiffness of the rear anti-roll bar. Stiffer means less body roll at the rear and more oversteer. Kunos documentation: the setup overwrites the anti-roll bars of the car file, unless ARB controllers are defined.

settings.label: Front anti-roll bar min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest front anti-roll bar stiffness allowed. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Front anti-roll bar max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest front anti-roll bar stiffness allowed. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Rear anti-roll bar min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest rear anti-roll bar stiffness allowed. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Rear anti-roll bar max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest rear anti-roll bar stiffness allowed. Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Front spring rate
settings.description: Default setup: wheel rate of the front springs (both wheels). Stiffer means less body roll and dive at the front and more understeer. Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the spring rate of the coilover file.

settings.label: Rear spring rate
settings.description: Default setup: wheel rate of the rear springs (both wheels). Stiffer means less body roll and squat at the rear and more oversteer. Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the spring rate of the coilover file.

settings.label: Front spring rate min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest front wheel rate allowed (both wheels). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Front spring rate max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest front wheel rate allowed (both wheels). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Rear spring rate min
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Lowest rear wheel rate allowed (both wheels). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Rear spring rate max
settings.description: Setup limit (range offered in the in-game setup screen, effect on the game not yet tested). Highest rear wheel rate allowed (both wheels). Kunos documentation: a setup value outside its limits is forced to the limit, which can make the car dysfunctional; even hidden options need limits that allow the setup value.

settings.label: Front ride height
settings.description: Default setup: target ride height of the front axle (setup aero.front_target_height). The spring collar positions (collar_front) realise the target height, so change them together; the effect on the handling is not confirmed. Kunos documentation: the collar positions of the setup are computed by the editor's Auto Setup from the ride height, and the ride height will become a result of other settings.

settings.label: Rear ride height
settings.description: Default setup: target ride height of the rear axle (setup aero.rear_target_height). The spring collar positions (collar_rear) realise the target height, so change them together; the effect on the handling is not confirmed. Kunos documentation: the collar positions of the setup are computed by the editor's Auto Setup from the ride height, and the ride height will become a result of other settings.

settings.label: Front spring collar position
settings.description: Default setup: position of the front spring collars (setup aero.collar_positions_mm, both front wheels), the values that realise the target ride height. Kunos documentation: the collar positions are computed by the editor's Auto Setup from the ride height and should not be adjusted manually. If you change them, change them together with ride_height_front.

settings.label: Rear spring collar position
settings.description: Default setup: position of the rear spring collars (setup aero.collar_positions_mm, both rear wheels), the values that realise the target ride height. Kunos documentation: the collar positions are computed by the editor's Auto Setup from the ride height and should not be adjusted manually. If you change them, change them together with ride_height_rear.

settings.label: Front bump stop up rate
settings.description: Default setup: rate (stiffness) of the "up" bump stop of the front axle (both wheels). Kunos documentation: bump stop up is the compression direction and its force is the bump stop spring rate; the setup overrides the bump stop force (rate) of the coilover file. Higher is stiffer; the unit is not confirmed, so none is shown. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Rear bump stop up rate
settings.description: Default setup: rate (stiffness) of the "up" bump stop of the rear axle (both wheels). Kunos documentation: bump stop up is the compression direction and its force is the bump stop spring rate; the setup overrides the bump stop force (rate) of the coilover file. Higher is stiffer; the unit is not confirmed, so none is shown. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Front bump stop down rate
settings.description: Default setup: rate (stiffness) of the "down" bump stop of the front axle (both wheels), the stop at the end of the wheel travel in that direction (assumed). Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the bump stop force (rate) of the coilover file. Higher is stiffer; the unit is not confirmed, so none is shown. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Rear bump stop down rate
settings.description: Default setup: rate (stiffness) of the "down" bump stop of the rear axle (both wheels), the stop at the end of the wheel travel in that direction (assumed). Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the bump stop force (rate) of the coilover file. Higher is stiffer; the unit is not confirmed, so none is shown. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Front bump stop up range
settings.description: Default setup: travel at which the "up" bump stop of the front axle (both wheels) engages. Kunos documentation: bump stop up is the compression direction and its range is the distance from the rest position to the bump stop; the setup overrides the bump stop range of the coilover file. The unit is not confirmed, probably metres (same magnitude as the coilover bump stop range); stock values can be negative. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Rear bump stop up range
settings.description: Default setup: travel at which the "up" bump stop of the rear axle (both wheels) engages. Kunos documentation: bump stop up is the compression direction and its range is the distance from the rest position to the bump stop; the setup overrides the bump stop range of the coilover file. The unit is not confirmed, probably metres (same magnitude as the coilover bump stop range); stock values can be negative. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Front bump stop down range
settings.description: Default setup: travel at which the "down" bump stop of the front axle (both wheels) engages. Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the bump stop range of the coilover file. The unit is not confirmed, probably metres (same magnitude as the coilover bump stop range); stock values can be negative. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Rear bump stop down range
settings.description: Default setup: travel at which the "down" bump stop of the rear axle (both wheels) engages. Kunos documentation: the setup overrides the bump stop range of the coilover file. The unit is not confirmed, probably metres (same magnitude as the coilover bump stop range); stock values can be negative. Effect in the game not confirmed.

settings.label: Front damper slow bump
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel moves up slowly (body roll and pitch) on the front axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Front damper fast bump
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel is pushed up quickly (bumps and kerbs) on the front axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Front damper slow rebound
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel moves down slowly (body roll and pitch) on the front axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Front damper fast rebound
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel drops quickly (after bumps and kerbs) on the front axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Rear damper slow bump
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel moves up slowly (body roll and pitch) on the rear axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Rear damper fast bump
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel is pushed up quickly (bumps and kerbs) on the rear axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Rear damper slow rebound
settings.description: Default setup: damper force when the wheel moves down slowly (body roll and pitch) on the rear axle (both wheels). Higher is firmer. Kunos documentation: cars with active dampers ignore the setup damper values, and cars with racing damper tables use a click number (a range such as 1 to 50) instead of force values.

settings.label: Front camber
settings.description: Default setup: front wheel tilt (both wheels). More negative tilts the top of the wheel inward, which gives more grip in corners and less on straights.

settings.label: Rear camber
settings.description: Default setup: rear wheel tilt (both wheels). More negative tilts the top of the wheel inward, which gives more cornering grip and less straight-line grip at the rear.

settings.label: Front toe
settings.description: Default setup: front wheel toe angle (both wheels). Sign convention assumed: a negative value points the fronts slightly outward.

settings.label: Rear toe
settings.description: Default setup: rear wheel toe angle (both wheels). Sign convention assumed: a positive value points the rears slightly inward.

settings.label: Front tyre pressure
settings.description: Default setup: cold pressure of the front tyres. Raising it stiffens the tyre; the effect on grip depends on the tyre model.

settings.label: Rear tyre pressure
settings.description: Default setup: cold pressure of the rear tyres. Raising it stiffens the tyre; the effect on grip depends on the tyre model.

settings.label: Front camber min

settings.label: Front tyre lateral grip
settings.description: Peak lateral (sideways) friction coefficient of the front tyre (TyresCompoundData.modelData.Dy0, a unitless mu; for example the stock road tyres of the BMW have about 1.2, the supercar tyres about 1.27). Assumed from the field name: a higher value gives the front axle more sideways grip; the real grip also depends on load, temperature, pressure and wear. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre longitudinal grip
settings.description: Peak longitudinal friction coefficient of the front tyre (modelData.Dx0, a unitless mu). Assumed from the field name: a higher value gives the front axle more grip when accelerating and braking. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre peak slip angle
settings.description: Slip angle at which the front tyre reaches its friction limit (modelData.friction_limit_angle, degrees, for example about 8 on the stock tyres of the BMW). Assumed from the field name: a larger angle lets the front axle keep gripping at bigger slip angles, so a slide builds up more progressively. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre load reference
settings.description: Reference vertical load of the front tyre model (modelData.Fz0, newtons; for example 3930 front and 4320 rear on the stock tyres of the BMW). Assumed from the field name: the grip coefficients are valid at this load and the grip changes with the load around it, so a different value moves the load at which the front tyre works best. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre inflation pressure (tyre file)
settings.description: Inflation pressure stored in the front tyre file (TyresCompoundData.pressure, for example 30 psi on the stock tyres of the BMW, between 23 and 30 on the other tested cars). The pressure you run is the setup value (tyre_pressure_front); how the two interact in the game is not confirmed. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre lateral flex stiffness
settings.description: Lateral flex stiffness of the front tyre (tyreData.lateralFlexK; the unit is not known; for example the stock tyres of the BMW have 30000 road and 38000 supercar). Assumed from the field name: a higher value makes the sidewall stiffer sideways, so the front tyre gives less. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. settings.label: Front tyre vertical stiffness

Assumed from the field name: a higher value is a stiffer tyre that compresses less under load, which also changes the ride of the front axle. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. settings.label: Front tyre heat partition
settings.description: Heat partition coefficient of the front tyre (thermalData.heat_partition_coeff; for example 0.7 on the stock road tyres and 0.9 on the supercar tyres of the BMW, 1.4 on the Porsche slicks, so it is not a plain fraction). Assumed from the field name: it sets how much of the friction heat goes into the tyre, so a higher value heats the front tyre faster when it slides. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre graining gain
settings.description: Strength of the graining (rubber balling on the surface) of the front tyre. Written to both thermalData.grainGain and thermalData.grainGamma, which are equal in every tyre of the game (for example 0.27 on the stock road tyres of the BMW, 0.47 on the supercar tyres). Assumed from the field names: a higher value makes the front tyre grain up more when it slides. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Front tyre graining slip angle gain

Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. settings.label: Front tyre thermal curve
settings.description: Thermal performance curve family of the front tyre (thermalData.thermalPerformanceCurve): a curve of the grip multiplier against tyre temperature in degrees Celsius. Each choice is one of the game's shared curve files, named without tcurve_ and .curve (content\cars\common_phsx\tyres\<folder>\tcurve_<choice>.curve); the build points the tyre at that file, no curve is copied. Read from the curve files: road holds full grip at about 32 to 70 degrees, supercar at about 60 to 95, slick at about 70 to 105; the other families have their own windows. A hotter window suits a tyre that is heated by sliding. Stored in the car's own copy of the front tyre file (data/tyres/<car id>_front.tyre), which the build makes only when a front tyre setting is changed. It changes the compound the car starts on; the other compounds in the game's tyre list stay stock. The effect on driving is not tested in the game.

settings.label: Starting fuel
settings.description: Default setup: fuel in the tank at the start. More fuel adds weight. Kunos documentation: the Fuel of the car file is overwritten by this setup value.

settings.label: Traction control level
settings.description: Default setup: traction control level (setup electronics.tc1), an index into the car's traction control levels. Kunos documentation: levels are counted from 0 and level 0 is the Setting 1 of the car; for the aid to be switchable off, the car must define Setting 1 as no intervention. Whether this car does is not confirmed. The performance (driving) modes store their own levels: driver_aids_off switches them off too. Only shown for cars whose stock setup stores this field.

settings.label: Traction control 2 level
settings.description: Default setup: level of the second traction control channel (setup electronics.tc2); 0 is assumed to be off, not confirmed. Kunos documentation: TC2 adjusts only the Engine Cut Level (lower is smoother and earlier) and leaves the other TC1 parameters unaffected. Only shown for cars whose stock setup stores this field.

settings.label: ABS level
settings.description: Default setup: ABS level (setup electronics.abs), an index into the car's ABS levels. Kunos documentation: levels are counted from 0; for the aid to be switchable off, the car must define its first level (Setting 1) as no intervention. Whether this car does is not confirmed. driver_aids_off does not change it. Only shown for cars whose stock setup stores this field.

settings.label: Driver aids off
settings.description: Switch: when on, traction control (tc1, tc2) and stability control (esc) are set to 0 in every performance (driving) mode of the car and in the setup defaults, so no driver aid steps in; ABS is not touched. Kunos documentation: levels are counted from 0 and the car must define Setting 1 (level 0) as no intervention for the aid to be switchable off; whether this car does is not confirmed. Fields the car does not store are not added.
